We welcomed our newest and youngest member into the team – Ben Flint – who won the pole vault in difficult conditions. Anyway, an excellent result and another one for the record books.
PV: 3, B.Flint 4.80.

Ben Flint, who was experiencing Belgrave's European adventures for the first time, played it safe and came into the pole vault competition at 4.80, which he failed twice much to the concern of the team managers.
Our happy wanderer would surely be with us by the time Ben Flint's poles had been checked through - always a lengthy operation.
In the pole vault Ben Flint secured a clear win over Ian Tullett thereby gaining selection for Athens. Not to be outdone the throws produced some interesting storylines.
Meanwhile, another double win in the pole vault, with the mature (that's a nice way of putting it) Mike Edwards proving a point with a fine 5.40 clearance ahead of Ben Flint.

In the triple jump, Philips Idowu leapt to 16.11 (no wind speed) and the vaulters achieved a valuable double with Mike Edwards again getting the better of Ben Flint and in so doing moved up the all time points list to fourth spot.
Two more wins in the pole vault and again Mike Edwards came out ahead of Ben Flint but only on countback this time. But back to the other outstanding performances.

Richard Aspden again gained solid points, while in the pole vault Ian Tullett equalled the winning height with a fine 5.20m effort, narrowly beating Ben Flint who was pleased to be competing again after injury.

Also in the long relay was pole vaulter Ben Flint who clocked 52.0 secs to partly atone for a disappointing 4.50m in the pole vault. He had been held up in traffic, used 4.50m as a warm up but then failed to clear heights which he would normally reach with his eyes shut (well almost!)
